introduction: North Carolina CIP assists qualifying households facing a health-related or life-threatening heating or cooling emergency.
description: North Carolina CIP assists qualifying households facing a health-related or life-threatening heating or cooling emergency.

sections.who: Income, resources, eligible household status and an energy crisis must be assessed. A past-due bill alone does not establish the health-related emergency.
sections.get: Assistance can help resolve qualifying energy emergencies while funds remain available.
sections.docs:
• Utility statement and amount owed.
  • Income and household information.
  • Requested eligibility records and crisis details.
sections.apply:
1. Contact county DSS

    Use CIP guidance or ePASS.

  2. Explain the danger

    Describe the household member’s risk and the heating or cooling problem.

  3. Submit proof

    Mail, email, fax or drop-off routes are listed; a face-to-face interview is not currently required.
sections.after: Keep the agency informed of emergency dates. Contact the utility separately.
sections.sources: Content checked October 1, 2026 using CIP eligibility and intake. Current eligibility and the final decision remain with the program.

faqs: Must I have a disconnect notice?
The state also accepts a final notice or past-due bill.
A qualifying energy-related health or life-threatening crisis is required.
